subject: community-medicine
title: Rabies Post-Exposure Regimens: Intradermal Protocols and Immunoglobulin

steps.title: Intradermal schedule: Updated Thai Red Cross regimen
steps.tx: The standard post-exposure vaccination protocol in Indian public hospitals is the **Updated Thai Red Cross regimen**, an evidence-based two-site intradermal schedule. On each of four scheduled clinic visits, specifically days zero, three, seven and twenty-eight, the patient receives zero point one millilitres of reconstituted vaccine intradermally at two distinct anatomical sites, creating a pale raised bleb over both the left and right deltoids.
steps.say: The Updated Thai Red Cross schedule gives two intradermal injections on days zero, three, seven and twenty-eight. A small pale bleb is raised over both deltoid muscles at each visit.

steps.title: Intramuscular Essen regimen comparison
steps.tx: In private clinical practice, physicians frequently administer the five-dose intramuscular **Essen regimen**, injecting one full reconstituted vial of zero point five or one point zero millilitres into the deltoid muscle on days zero, three, seven, fourteen and twenty-eight. Intramuscular injections into the gluteal area are strictly prohibited because thick subcutaneous gluteal fat slows vascular absorption and significantly impairs the neutralising antibody response.
steps.say: The intramuscular Essen regimen injects a full vial into the shoulder on days zero, three, seven, fourteen and twenty-eight. Gluteal injections are forbidden because buttocks fat blunts antibody production.

left.title: Intradermal (2-site TRC)
points: Uses 0.2 ml total vaccine per visit

right.title: Intramuscular (5-dose Essen)
points: Uses 1 full vial (0.5 to 1.0 ml) per visit
Total volume 2.5 to 5.0 ml across therapy

steps.title: Rabies immunoglobulin: equine versus human
steps.tx: In Category III bites, administering **rabies immunoglobulin** provides immediate passive neutralising antibodies at the wound site, bridging the critical seven to ten-day immunological gap before active vaccine antibodies appear in circulation. Equine rabies immunoglobulin is administered at forty international units per kilogram body weight, whereas human rabies immunoglobulin is administered at twenty international units per kilogram without requiring prior skin sensitivity testing.
steps.say: Rabies immunoglobulin provides immediate protection during the first week before vaccine antibodies develop. The dose is twenty units per kilogram for human product and forty for equine.

rows: Skin testing no longer routinely required
No sensitivity test needed; zero serum sickness
Synthetic consistency; no animal biological risk

steps.title: Immunoglobulin infiltration technique
steps.tx: Proper administration technique mandates thorough **wound infiltration**, injecting as much of the weight-calculated immunoglobulin dose as anatomically safe directly into and around the depths and margins of every bite wound. If the wound is small or extensive, the calculated volume may be diluted with sterile normal saline to ensure complete infiltration, with any leftover product injected intramuscularly at a site distant from the vaccine.
steps.say: Inject as much immunoglobulin as possible directly into and around all the animal bite wounds. Any remaining medication is given as an intramuscular shot far from the vaccine arm.

nodes.label: Calculate total RIG dose by body weight
Infiltrate thoroughly into all bite wounds
Inject any surplus IM distant from vaccine

steps.title: Re-exposure protocol in previously vaccinated individuals
steps.tx: When a person with documented prior completion of a full pre-exposure or post-exposure rabies course experiences a new animal bite, the protocol for **re-exposure vaccination** requires immediate soap-and-water wound washing. Rabies immunoglobulin is never administered because memory B cells respond immediately, requiring only two booster vaccine doses on day zero and day three (one site intradermally or one dose intramuscularly) to restore immunity.
steps.say: Patients previously vaccinated against rabies need only two booster shots on days zero and three after a new bite. They never receive immunoglobulin because their immune memory wakes up rapidly.

left.title: Unimmunised individual
points: Mandatory RIG infiltration for Category III
Takes 7 to 10 days to produce antibodies

right.title: Documented prior vaccinee
points: Only 2 booster doses on days 0 and 3
Anamnestic IgG surge within 48 to 72 hours

steps.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis indications and schedule
steps.tx: High-risk occupational cohorts receive **pre-exposure prophylaxis** to establish baseline immunity before potential occupational exposure. Designated candidates include veterinarians, dog catchers, animal handlers, wildlife sanctuary rangers, and laboratory technicians handling live Lyssavirus cultures, receiving zero point one millilitres of vaccine intradermally at one site (or one intramuscular dose) on days zero, seven, and twenty-one or twenty-eight.
steps.say: Veterinarians, animal handlers and rabies laboratory workers receive pre-exposure vaccination on days zero, seven, and twenty-one. This protects against unrecognised exposures.

rows: Two booster doses on days 0 and 3; no RIG
Booster if virus neutralising titre < 0.5 IU/ml
Two booster doses on days 0 and 3; no RIG

steps.title: Leptospirosis zoonosis and transmission ecology
steps.tx: Another dangerous zoonotic infection striking agrarian and urban populations is **leptospirosis transmission**, caused by spirochaetes of the species Leptospira interrogans. Pathogenic leptospires colonize the proximal renal tubules of reservoir animals, primarily domestic rats and cattle, shedding viable bacteria into animal urine that contaminates monsoon rainwater puddles, sewer overflows, flooded paddy fields and waterlogged urban roads, penetrating abraded human skin.
steps.say: Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection spread through rat and cattle urine. During monsoon floods, spirochaetes in waterlogged streets enter the body through small cuts in the skin.

nodes.label: Rodent renal carrier sheds leptospires in urine
Entry via abraded skin or conjunctiva

steps.title: Severe leptospirosis and Weil disease
steps.tx: While ninety percent of leptospirosis presentations run a self-limiting anicteric febrile illness, ten percent progress to severe icteric disease known as **Weil disease**. Manifestations include severe hepatic jaundice, acute oliguric renal failure from interstitial nephritis, severe thrombocytopenia with haemorrhagic diathesis, and life-threatening pulmonary haemorrhage; prominent bilateral conjunctival suffusion without purulent discharge serves as a pathognomonic diagnostic clue.
steps.say: Severe leptospirosis, or Weil disease, causes jaundice, kidney failure, bleeding and lung haemorrhage. Bloodshot red eyes without any pus provide an essential diagnostic clue.

left.title: Anicteric leptospirosis (90%)
points: Sudden fever, headache and calf myalgia

right.title: Severe Weil disease (10%)
points: Deep jaundice and acute kidney failure
High case fatality requiring intensive dialysis

steps.title: Chemoprophylaxis and post-flood outbreak response
steps.tx: During widespread monsoon inundations and urban floods, disaster management protocols provide **doxycycline chemoprophylaxis** to rescue workers, sanitation personnel and agricultural labourers wading through contaminated waters. A prophylactic dose of two hundred milligrams of oral doxycycline is given once weekly during periods of high exposure, while confirmed clinical cases receive prompt therapeutic regimens of intravenous penicillin G or ceftriaxone.
steps.say: Rescue workers and flood victims take two hundred milligrams of doxycycline once weekly to prevent leptospirosis. Severe cases are treated in hospital with intravenous penicillin or ceftriaxone.

rows: 1.5 million units IV every 6 hours for 7 days
